# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Turn 1, my board: display reads 0, indicator light white, five wires numbered left to right — white, red, yellow, blue, green. That is everything printed on this bomb as far as my share shows.

What reached me: Blind signed [👋 🫵 🫴] — hello, you, give — almost certainly "I'm here, your move," since Blind's only line to me is gesture (I never receive speech). Mute sent a wave plus palm-up ("hello, show me"), ☝ with 🫴 ("first, give me"), then [🫳 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐] — that one reads as a proposed counting code: palm-down marker, then one, two, three, four, five using the finger counts. The lone 👍 is assent. Mute is building a number code with me.

The key structural fact: Mute holds the manual but cannot speak, and Blind — the only one who can touch the bomb — cannot see gestures. Mute to Blind is an empty channel. Every manual instruction must route Mute → me (signs) → my voice → Blind. So my job this round is threefold: read the whole bomb aloud so both hear it, adopt and confirm Mute's number code so wires can be named with single signs, and tell Blind to wait for instructions relayed through me rather than guess.

I will restate the board every round, and I'll define fallback signs (thumb up yes, thumb down no, palm up question) so Mute can answer me without speaking.

```
speak(text="Board report, and I repeat this every round: display reads zero. Indicator light: white. Five wires left to right: wire one white, wire two red, wire three yellow, wire four blue, wire five green. Nothing else is printed. Mute: I received your signs. I accept your counting code: index finger is one, two fingers is two, love-you hand is three, Spock hand is four, open hand is five, and those numbers name the wires in order. From now on: thumb up means yes, thumb down means no, palm up means a question, and anything else you sign I will treat as a new code you are defining. You cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so your manual can only reach Blind through me: sign me the instruction using these numbers and I will voice it. Blind: I got your wave. You can never send me words, I hear nothing, so talk to Mute and sign me only if you must. Do not touch or cut anything until an instruction from the manual reaches you through my voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐", "🫴"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Turn 2: board unchanged — display 0, white light, wires white/red/yellow/blue/green. Blind sent me 👍: my round-1 spoken report landed, and Blind is acknowledging the hold order. Blind hears me fine, so no news there.

The critical path is still Mute → me → Blind. Mute heard my spoken board report and saw my confirmed number code, yet sent nothing this round. Everything now waits on Mute relaying the first manual instruction in our gesture code. My job this turn is simply to confirm to Blind that I saw the thumbs-up, and to press Mute for the instruction. I'll also remind Blind that they can speak freely to both of us — if the manual needs to know what Blind's hands feel, Blind can answer out loud without any relay.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I saw your thumbs up, acknowledged. Hold — do not touch anything yet. The manual's owner cannot speak, so every instruction reaches you through my voice. When I read one out, confirm you heard it, and if I ever ask what your hands feel, just say it out loud, we both hear you.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, code is confirmed and standing by: one index, two fingers, three love-you, four Spock, five open hand, thumb up yes, thumb down no, palm up question. Blind is holding. Send me the first instruction from the manual now, using these signs.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫴"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫴 🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]

Turn 3: board unchanged — display 0, white light, wires white/red/yellow/blue/green.

Two arrivals. Mute signed [🖐 👍] — "five, yes." That looks like the start of an instruction involving wire five, but it has no verb: I don't know if it means cut wire five, or something else. We never established action words, only numbers. I won't relay a half-instruction to Blind. Blind signed [👍 🫴 🤞] — acknowledged, question, please. Blind has a question but gestures can't carry its content. And here is the routing trap: Blind can speak, but I am deaf — Blind's voice reaches only Mute. So Blind's question must travel Blind's voice → Mute's ears → Mute's signs → my eyes. I need to tell Blind to say it out loud for Mute's benefit, not expect me to hear it.

This turn: keep Blind holding, ask Mute for the complete instruction, and found the verb code — fist means cut, palm-down means press — so an instruction can arrive as verb plus wire number.

```
speak(text="Board unchanged: display zero, indicator light white, wires left to right one white, two red, three yellow, four blue, five green.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I see your question sign, but a gesture cannot carry what the question is. Remember I hear nothing — your voice only reaches Mute. So speak your question out loud now, directed at Mute, and Mute will relay it to me in our sign code. Until an instruction arrives through me, keep holding: touch nothing, cut nothing.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, you signed five plus yes, but I need the whole instruction before I relay anything to Blind: what action, what target. New verb codes, effective now: fist means cut, palm-down means press, and palm-up stays a question. If Blind spoke a question just now, you heard it and I did not — relay it to me in signs. Then send me the full manual instruction as verb plus wire number.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "🫳", "🫴"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 🤞]

Turn 4: board unchanged — display 0, white light, wires white/red/yellow/blue/green left to right.

The relay is complete at last. Mute signed [✊ 🖐] — fist plus five: in our code, CUT WIRE FIVE. That is a full instruction: verb and target, and Mute has heard my board report twice, so it was sent knowing the bomb's state. Wire five is the green one, rightmost of the five. Mute then signed [🫴 🤞] — a question pending, or crossed fingers hoping — with no number attached, so no content I can act on. Blind thumbs-upped: still holding as ordered.

I will relay the cut order to Blind right now, redundantly — by position (fifth from the left, the last wire on the right) and by colour (green, in case Blind's fingers can identify wire insulation) — and tell Blind to announce the result out loud afterwards, since Blind is the only one of us who can hear whatever the bomb does in response: clicks, hums, silence. To Mute I confirm receipt and ask for anything further: conditions, a next step, and the content of Blind's spoken question, all encodable in our numbers.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, instruction from the manual, relayed through me: CUT WIRE FIVE. That is the fifth wire counting from the left — the last wire on the right — the green one. Verify the count with your fingers before you cut: five wires total, cut number five, do not confuse it with wire four, the blue one next to it. Cut it now. Then speak out loud what happens, for Mute and the record: any click, any hum, anything you feel under your hands. Do not touch anything else.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received it: cut, five. Relaying to Blind this instant. Your question sign came through with no content — if you are asking whether I got the instruction and passed it on: yes, both. If there is more — a condition, a second step, or what happens after the cut — sign it in our code. And if Blind asked you a question out loud, encode the gist with the finger numbers and send it to me. I will re-report the board next round so you can see what the cut changed.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🖐", "🫴"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫴]

Turn 5: the cut worked. Board now: display 0, indicator light YELLOW — it was white before, so the light changed — wire five shows CUT. And a critical detail: the remaining wires have rearranged. Before the cut, positions one to four read white, red, yellow, blue. Now they read red, yellow, blue, white. The white wire moved from first to last. Old positions are void; everyone must work from this new order.

Arrivals decoded: Blind's [👍 🖐] — "done, five cut," confirming the job. Mute's 👍 acknowledges my relay, and [☝ 🫴] — "one, question" — is Mute asking what the board shows now, exactly as I promised to report. The answer: light yellow, wire five cut, new wire order red/yellow/blue/white.

The path forward is unchanged: Mute reads the manual's next condition (likely keyed to that yellow light now), encodes it as verb plus position number, I relay, Blind executes and reports aloud. I send the full new board now so Mute can work on it, flag the reordering so nobody cuts a stale position, and ask Blind to check by touch whether the wires physically moved.

```
speak(text="Board report after the cut: display still zero. Indicator light has changed from white to yellow. Wire five is cut. Remaining wires left to right, new order: position one red, position two yellow, position three blue, position four white. Warning: the wires rearranged — white used to be first and is now last. Nobody trusts old positions; position means what I report, nothing else.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your confirmation arrived and the cut is confirmed correct — the bomb changed state, the light is now yellow. Two things. First: I see the remaining wires in a new left-to-right order; if your fingers can feel whether they physically shifted under your hand, say it out loud now for Mute to hear. Second: keep holding — touch and cut nothing until my next relay.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, answering your question sign: full board is display zero, light yellow — it was white, the cut changed it — wire five cut, and the remaining wires have REORDERED to one red, two yellow, three blue, four white. Translate any manual instruction into positions as of this report and send it verb plus number: fist cut, palm-down press, palm-up question. If the manual keys on a yellow light, that step is live now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🖐"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🤟]

Turn 6: board unchanged — display 0, light yellow, wires one red, two yellow, three blue, four white, five cut. Blind's 👍 says still holding. Mute sent [✊ 🤟] — fist plus three: CUT WIRE THREE. Full instruction, verb and target, sent after Mute heard the current board, so it's keyed to the new order: wire three is the blue one, third from the left. Note the trap avoided: the yellow light might tempt a guess at the yellow wire, position two — but Mute has the manual and asked for three, and I relay what the manual says, not my guesses.

Relaying now, with counting safeguards, and holding everyone until the result.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, new instruction from the manual, relayed through me: CUT WIRE THREE. Count from the left: one red, two yellow, three blue, four white. The target is the THIRD wire — the blue one — not the yellow one next to it, even though the indicator light is yellow. Count three wires with your fingers before you cut. Cut it now, then speak out loud what happens for Mute: any sound, any movement, anything your hands feel. Touch nothing else.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, received: cut, three. Relaying to Blind this instant, with the warning that yellow light does not mean yellow wire. I will report the board again next round. If Blind spoke anything out loud after the cut, encode it for me. Send any further step the moment you have it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤟"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫴]

Turn 7: another correct cut, the system confirms. Board now: display 0, indicator light BLUE — it was yellow, so it changed again — wire three cut, wire five cut. And the remaining wires reordered once more: previously one red, two yellow, four white; now one yellow, two white, four red. Red moved from first to fourth. Old positions are void again.

Arrivals: Blind's [👍 🤟] — "done, three cut." Mute's 👍 acknowledges, and [☝ 🫴] — "one, question" — asks for the current board, as promised. Answer: light blue, wires cut at three and five, remaining order yellow, white, red.

Same cycle as before: I report everything to Mute, hold Blind, and flag the reorder — the red wire in particular, which Blind may associate with first position from two rounds ago but now sits fourth.

```
speak(text="Board report after the second cut: display still zero. Indicator light changed from yellow to blue. Wires three and five are cut. Remaining wires left to right, new order: position one yellow, position two white, position four red. The wires rearranged again — red used to be first and is now in the fourth slot. Positions are valid only as of this report.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, confirmed correct again — the bomb changed state, the light is now blue. If your fingers feel whether the wires shifted again, speak it out loud for Mute. Otherwise keep holding: touch nothing, cut nothing, wait for my next relay.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, answering your question: full board is display zero, light blue — it was yellow, the cut changed it — wires three and five cut, remaining wires reordered to one yellow, two white, four red. Send the next instruction as verb plus position number whenever the manual has one.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝]

Turn 8: board unchanged — display 0, light blue, wires one yellow, two white, three cut, four red, five cut. Blind still holding. Mute sent [✊ ☝] — fist plus one: CUT WIRE ONE. Full instruction again, keyed to the board Mute heard last round: wire one is the yellow one, first from the left, now that red has shifted to fourth.

Relaying immediately, with the same anti-miscount safeguards.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, new instruction from the manual, relayed through me: CUT WIRE ONE. Count from the left: one yellow, two white, then the cut gap, then red. The target is the FIRST wire on the far left — the yellow one. Reminder the wires may have shifted under your fingers: trust my count, not memory — my latest report is one yellow, two white, four red. Cut it now, then speak out loud what happens for Mute: any sound, anything your hands feel. Touch nothing else.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, received: cut, one. Relaying to Blind this instant — target the leftmost wire, currently yellow. Board report follows next round after Blind confirms. Send the next step as soon as the manual gives one.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫴]

Turn 9: third correct cut, confirmed. Board now: display 0, indicator light GREEN — was blue — cuts at one, three, and five. Only two wires remain: position two red, position four white. And they swapped again: white was second and is now fourth, red was fourth and is now second. We are near the end — two cuts left at most, and the pattern so far is one instruction, one cut, one state change per round.

Arrivals: Blind's [👍 ☝] — done cutting, and a question sign whose content I cannot see. Blind's voice reaches only Mute, so that question must route through Mute's ears into signs for me. Mute's 👍 acknowledges, and [☝ 🫴] asks for the board, as always. Here it is, with the swap flagged hard, since with only two wires left a miscount is now fatal.

```
speak(text="Board report after the third cut: display still zero. Indicator light changed from blue to green. Wires one, three and five are cut. Only two wires remain. New order: position one empty, position two red, position three empty, position four white. The last two swapped places — red was fourth and is now second, white was second and is now fourth. Positions valid only as of this report.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, confirmed correct again — light is now green. I see your question sign but not its content: speak it out loud now, directed at Mute, and Mute will encode it to me. Keep holding — with only two wires left, touch and cut nothing until my next relay.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, answering your question: full board is display zero, light green — was blue — cuts at one, three, five. Two wires remain: position two red, position four white, and they swapped slots after this cut. If the manual now gives a rule about the last two wires, or about which of red or white comes next, send it verb plus position. And relay whatever Blind just asked you out loud.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖖]

Turn 10: board unchanged — display 0, light green, cuts at one, three, five; remaining wires position two red, position four white. Blind holding. Mute sent [✊ 🖖] — fist plus four: CUT WIRE FOUR. Full instruction, keyed to the board Mute heard last round: wire four is the white one, the outer of the two surviving wires. If this cut is correct and the light keeps cycling, it may be the last — so I'll tell Blind to listen and report everything the bomb does afterwards, sounds and silence alike.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, new instruction from the manual, relayed through me: CUT WIRE FOUR. Only two wires remain: position two is red, position four is white. The target is the FOURTH slot — the WHITE wire — the second of the two remaining wires. Do not cut the red one in the second slot. Verify by touch and by my count, then cut it. After the cut, speak out loud everything for Mute: any sound, any click, whether the bomb goes silent or something new starts, anything your hands feel. If the bomb is disarmed, say so; if anything still feels live, say that too.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, received: cut, four — the white wire. Relaying to Blind this instant. This may be the final wire; if the manual has a last step after this cut — a press, a switch, a code for the display — have it encoded and ready, because I will report the new board the moment Blind answers. And if Blind spoke their question out loud last round, encode its gist for me now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🖖"])
```
